And signage reads: About "Luminaria"
In 2019, the Art in Public Places Program of New Mexico Arts issued a national request for an exterior, site-specific commission project to be located at the Steve.Schiff District Attorney Building in Albuquerque, New Mexico, funded by a special appropriation made by the State Legislature. The group ROBD (Repeat Offenders Bring Death, Destruction and Devastation) made up of local families of the victims of gun violence worked with Senator Daniel A. Ivey-Soto and Representative Nate Gentry to secure funding the project.
The purpose of the commission was to create a non-traditional memorial that would provide a contemplative, healing, and uplifting space for victims and families dealing with the trauma of gun violence. Gordon Huether's concept, Luminaria, was chosen for its ability to convey the ideas of humanity, comfort, serenity, joy, and love. The memorial was inspired by several local traditions including luminarias, descansos (roadside memorials), and Mexican papel picado banners, with the shape of the sculptures referencing the native barrel cactus. "Luminaria" consists of three different sized sculptures and references a significant tradition in New Mexico: brown paper bags with cut out patterns, weighted down by sand and illuminated by candles from
within.
The shape is comprised of eight long "petals," each of which contain visual elements often found at descansos such as doves, flowers, sunbursts, hearts, teddy bears, praying hands, candles, and butterflies; thus drawing inspiration from humanity and the traditions that have helped communities cope in times of hardship. The three sculptures are each a different color, inspired by the vibrant barrel cactus flowers and colorful papel picado folk art. The sculptures are illuminated from within like lanterns, shining as a beacon of joy and love for all those in suffering, both day and night. The sculpture was dedicated in August 2021 and is now part of Bernalillo County's Public Art Collection.

The overall concept and design of the three large mosaic works and the six block long wall with gardens and rock work is dedicated with prayerful intent to the regeneration and renewal of the extinct, endangered and migratory species and their habitats in our bio-region. The park of native species and the rocks created at the north end of the design were chosen to represent the northern climate and terrain of our region in the Rocky Mountain chain. The MOUNTAIN HOME mosaic is dedicated especially to our mountains and the flora and fauna most at home in our northern areas. The central mosaic, RIVER HOME, content is dedicated to the creatures and plants of our central regions and our healing waters. The mosaic at the southern end, SUN HOME, with its native park is dedicated to the biodiversity and health of that geography.
